t: What stands here is the tower of St Alban, Wood Street, all that is left of a church of medieval origin. It was rebuilt in 1634, destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666, and then rebuilt again, this time to a Gothic design by Sir Christopher Wren. Wren was responsible for rebuilding fifty-two City churches after the fire, and he is also famous for St Paul's Cathedral, completed in 1710. Bombing in the Second World War severely damaged the church, and when the ruins were cleared, only the tower remained.
